title: Request routing callpath in pkg/api/
answers: How does a request get routed to a handler in pkg/api?
Why can route declarations reference hs.SomeService before the mux exists?
body:
HTTPServer.Run (pkg/api/http_server.go:462) → applyRoutes (http_server.go:677) → addMiddlewaresAndStaticRoutes (http_server.go:686) then hs.RouteRegister.Register(...) flushes the deferred route tree onto the real mux.

Route table: registerRoutes() at pkg/api/api.go:65 (~550 lines). Small routes declared inline (r.Get(...), apiRoute.Group(...)); larger features delegate, e.g. hs.registerFolderAPI to pkg/api/folder.go:25, hs.registerPlaylistAPI to pkg/api/playlist.go:23.

routing.Wrap (pkg/api/routing/routing.go:17) adapts a func(*contextmodel.ReqContext) response.Response into a raw web.Handler via res.WriteTo(c); typical route line is routing.Wrap(hs.GetDashboard).

RouteRegisterImpl (pkg/api/routing/route_register.go:74) just accumulates routes into a tree until Register() is called once at startup, which is why declarations can reference hs fields before the mux exists, and why duplicate (pattern, method) pairs panic at startup (route_register.go:154) instead of silently overriding.

Handler example: func (hs *HTTPServer) GetDashboard(c *contextmodel.ReqContext) response.Response at pkg/api/dashboard.go:69.
